theorem_title: Equal shortcut parity prefixes force equal dyadic residues
natural_language_statement:
Let $T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be the shortcut Collatz map: $T(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $T(n)=(3n+1)/2$ for odd $n$. Write $T^k$ for its $k$-fold iterate, with $T^0(n)=n$. The starts $n,m\in\mathbb N$ have the same parity prefix of length $k\in\mathbb N$ when $T^i(n)\equiv T^i(m)\pmod2$ for every $i<k$.

If the parity prefixes of $n$ and $m$ agree for $k$ steps, then

$$
n\equiv m\pmod{2^k}.
$$

This constrains finite parity-prefix collisions without a convergence assumption.
